issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a no-argument method messageOnRide() on the Rideable interface (and the template Main calls r.messageOnRide()), but the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and updates Pig and Seal to implement a method that requires an equipment parameter. This parameter mismatch breaks the intended API from the problem/template, will cause compilation errors if students follow the template signatures, and creates confusion about the required method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable API consistent across artifacts. Either (A) revert the solution to the problem/template specification by changing Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) to messageOnRide() and update Pig and Seal implementations to provide messageOnRide() that return "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", or (B) if an equipment parameter is intended, update the problem statement and template Main to describe and call messageOnRide(String equipment) (and update example calls in Main accordingly). Prefer (A) to match the UML and textual specification in the problem statement.

issues.description: The Rideable interface's messageOnRide method is defined with different signatures across artifacts: the problem statement (UML) and the template Main usage expect a no-argument method messageOnRide(), while the solution introduces a parameterized signature messageOnRide(String equipment). This changes the conceptual contract of the Rideable behavior and creates a mapping and compilation mismatch for students following the problem/template (who will call r.messageOnRide() with no argument) versus the solution implementation (which requires an argument).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable.messageOnRide signature consistent across all artifacts. Preferably change the solution to use the no-argument signature messageOnRide() and update Pig and Seal implementations to return "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" with no parameters, so it matches the UML and the template Main usage. Alternatively, if an equipment parameter is desired pedagogically, update the problem statement and template examples to include the parameter in the interface and all call sites.
